summary: Coffin Rock: a 60-ft Aermotor from 1921, raised to 86 ft in 1939, felled by a 1985 tornado; the 93-ft Aermotor of 1987 appears to still stand.

facts.status_note: The 1987 tower appears to stand. The 1921 tower was destroyed in 1985, and the Former Fire Lookout Sites entry says that earlier tower is no longer standing.

events.note: 60-foot steel Aermotor tower, with a cabin at its base for a local forestry man
J.M. Hall of Renovo was selected to live at the tower and man it around the clock
Express piece promoted the view as one of the best in the state
93-foot Aermotor steel tower with a full catwalk, constructed by the Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry; NHLR lists the build year as 1987
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register as the site of the 1921 tower
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register

corrections.why: The NHLR describes the 1987 tower as 93 feet (about 28.3 m). 30.5 m is 100 feet.
No source found for a 2018 replacement. The NHLR and the Express both date the replacement to 1987, two years after the 1985 tornado.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites entry says the tower is no longer standing. That refers to the 1921 tower, destroyed in 1985. The NHLR and the April 2024 Express article describe the 1987 tower as standing.
Heights differ by period: 60 feet in 1921, 86 feet after the 1939 raise, about 80 feet in a 1958 survey description, and 93 feet for the 1987 tower. The story uses 93 feet for the current tower.

notes_for_editor: Core history (1921 tower, 1985 tornado, 1987 replacement) agrees across four sources. Current access and climbing rules were not found. The 2018 replacement in the brief has no source. The brief's 30.5 m is 100 ft; the NHLR gives 93 ft. The Express article date (April 20, 2024) is printed in the article text. No new photos were checked.
